import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Rosa's conjecture

Rosa's conjecture says that all triangular cacti are graceful or nearly-graceful.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia/Graceful_labeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_labeling)
- [Wikipedia/List of unsolved problems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia/Cactus_graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cactus_graph)
- A. Rosa, *Cyclic Steiner triple systems and labelings of triangular cacti*,
  Scientia 1 (1988), 87–95.
- J. A. Gallian, *A dynamic survey of graph labeling*,
  [Electron. J. Combin. DS6](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/DS6).
-/

namespace RosasConjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]

/-- The label that a vertex labeling `f` induces on the edge `s(u, v)`, namely $|f(u) - f(v)|$. -/
def edgeLabel (f : V → ℕ) : Sym2 V → ℕ :=
  Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => ((f u : ℤ) - f v).natAbs, fun u v => by
    dsimp only
    rw [← Int.natAbs_neg, neg_sub]⟩

/-- A graph with $m$ edges is *graceful* if its vertices can be labeled injectively with
integers from $\{0, \dots, m\}$ so that the induced edge labels $|f(u) - f(v)|$ are exactly
$\{1, \dots, m\}$. -/
def IsGraceful : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℕ, Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ v, f v ≤ G.edgeFinset.card) ∧
    G.edgeFinset.image (edgeLabel f) = Finset.Icc 1 G.edgeFinset.card

/-- A graph with $m$ edges is *near-graceful* (or *nearly graceful*) if its vertices can be
labeled injectively with integers from $\{0, \dots, m + 1\}$ so that each edge is uniquely
identified by its induced label $|f(u) - f(v)|$, i.e. distinct edges get distinct labels.
(These labels then automatically lie in $\{1, \dots, m + 1\}$.) -/
def IsNearGraceful : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℕ, Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ v, f v ≤ G.edgeFinset.card + 1) ∧
    Set.InjOn (edgeLabel f) G.edgeSet

/-- A *triangular cactus* is a connected graph all of whose blocks are triangles.
Equivalently, it is a connected graph in which every edge lies on a cycle (i.e. no edge is a
bridge) and every cycle is a triangle (has length `3`).

Note that this includes the trivial one-vertex graph (which has no edges and is trivially
graceful). -/
def IsTriangularCactus : Prop :=
  G.Connected ∧ (∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ¬ G.IsBridge e) ∧
    ∀ ⦃v : V⦄ (p : G.Walk v v), p.IsCycle → p.length = 3

variable {G}

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsGraceful.isNearGraceful (h : IsGraceful G) : IsNearGraceful G := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hle, himg⟩ := h
  refine ⟨f, hf, fun v => (hle v).trans (Nat.le_succ _), ?_⟩
  rw [← coe_edgeFinset, ← Finset.card_image_iff, himg]
  simp

/-- The triangle is a triangular cactus. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isTriangularCactus_top_fin_three : IsTriangularCactus (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) := by
  refine ⟨connected_top, fun e he => ?_, fun v p hp => ?_⟩
  · induction e using Sym2.ind with
    | h a b =>
      rw [isBridge_iff, not_and, not_not, reachable_delete_edges_iff_exists_walk]
      intro hab
      obtain ⟨c, hca, hcb⟩ : ∃ c : Fin 3, c ≠ a ∧ c ≠ b := by
        clear he hab; revert a b; decide
      refine ⟨Walk.cons (by simpa using hca.symm) (Walk.cons (by simpa using hcb) Walk.nil), ?_⟩
      simp [hca.symm, hcb.symm]
  · refine le_antisymm ?_ hp.three_le_length
    have := hp.support_nodup.length_le_card
    simpa [Walk.length_support] using this

/-- The triangle is graceful: label its vertices `0`, `1`, `3`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isGraceful_top_fin_three : IsGraceful (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) := by
  refine ⟨![0, 1, 3], by decide, by decide, ?_⟩
  decide

/--
**Rosa's conjecture.** Every triangular cactus (a connected graph all of whose blocks are
triangles) is graceful or nearly-graceful.

Here a graph with $m$ edges is *graceful* if its vertices can be labeled injectively with
integers from $\{0, \dots, m\}$ so that the induced edge labels $|f(u) - f(v)|$ are exactly
$\{1, \dots, m\}$, and it is *nearly-graceful* if its vertices can be labeled injectively with
integers from $\{0, \dots, m + 1\}$ so that each edge is uniquely identified by its induced
label $|f(u) - f(v)|$ (which then lies in $\{1, \dots, m + 1\}$).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem rosas_conjecture (hG : IsTriangularCactus G) : IsGraceful G ∨ IsNearGraceful G := by
  sorry

/--
Rosa's original (1988) formulation is sharper: a triangular cactus with $t$ triangles is graceful
when $t \equiv 0, 1 \pmod 4$, and nearly-graceful when $t \equiv 2, 3 \pmod 4$ (in the latter
case it has $3t \equiv 1, 2 \pmod 4$ edges and is Eulerian, so it cannot be graceful by Rosa's
parity theorem). This variant records the graceful half; the nearly-graceful half is contained in
`rosas_conjecture`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem rosas_conjecture.variants.graceful [DecidableEq V] (hG : IsTriangularCactus G)
    (ht : (G.cliqueFinset 3).card % 4 = 0 ∨ (G.cliqueFinset 3).card % 4 = 1) :
    IsGraceful G := by
  sorry

end RosasConjecture

I followed the notes' fixed (Wikipedia) definition of near-graceful; note only that it is slightly weaker than the Gallian/Rosa notion (which requires the edge-label set to be {1..m} or {1..m-1,m+1}), so a reviewer may wish to decide whether the stricter notion is preferable for the Rosa (1988) formulation.
modeling_decisions: Literal reading kept: the conclusion is the disjunction `IsGraceful G ∨ IsNearGraceful G`, exactly as the Wikipedia list entry says. Since graceful implies near-graceful (proved in the file as the API lemma `IsGraceful.isNearGraceful`), this is logically equivalent to 'every triangular cactus is near-graceful'. Rosa's sharper 1988 form (t ≡ 0,1 mod 4 ⇒ graceful) is recorded separately as the variant `rosas_conjecture.variants.graceful`, sourced from Gallian's Dynamic Survey; its near-graceful half is already contained in the main statement so it is not repeated.

Near-graceful uses the Wikipedia article's definition (as fixed by the decomposition notes): injective labels in {0..m+1} with pairwise distinct edge labels (`Set.InjOn (edgeLabel f) G.edgeSet`); the range condition 1 ≤ label ≤ m+1 is automatic and hence not repeated. Note Gallian/Rosa use a slightly stricter notion (induced edge labels equal {1..m} or {1..m-1, m+1}); the Wikipedia notion is weaker, so with it the main statement is a (very slightly) weaker conjecture than Rosa's original. Graceful uses the standard 'edge labels are exactly {1..m}' (Finset.image = Finset.Icc 1 m), matching the existing repo file GracefulLabeling.lean.

Triangular cactus ('connected graph all of whose blocks are triangles') is encoded without a notion of block, which Mathlib lacks, as: `G.Connected ∧ (∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ¬ G.IsBridge e) ∧ ∀ v (p : G.Walk v v), p.IsCycle → p.length = 3`. Equivalence: bridgeless ⇒ every block is 2-connected on ≥ 3 vertices; if such a block contained a vertex outside one of its triangles, the fan lemma gives a cycle of length ≥ 4, so every block is a triangle; conversely, if all blocks are triangles then no edge is a bridge and every cycle (which lies in a single block) is a triangle. This also implies the Wikipedia cactus-graph definition (each edge in at most one cycle), since two triangles sharing an edge form a 4-cycle.

Degenerate case: the one-vertex graph K1 satisfies `IsTriangularCactus` vacuously (Rosa's block definition would exclude it, since its only block is K1). It is trivially graceful (m = 0, `Icc 1 0 = ∅`), so including it does not change the claim; documented in the definition's docstring. The empty vertex type is excluded by `Connected`.

Finiteness via `[Fintype V]` plus `[DecidableRel G.Adj]` so that `G.edgeFinset` (the edge count m) is available. `[DecidableEq V]` is only assumed on the variant (needed for `cliqueFinset 3`, which counts the triangles t; in a triangular cactus the 3-cliques are exactly the blocks).

Edge labels are computed by the bespoke `edgeLabel f : Sym2 V → ℕ := Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => |(f u : ℤ) - f v|.natAbs, _⟩`, mirroring the inline construction in FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/GracefulLabeling.lean.

Sanity tests included: K3 is a triangular cactus and is graceful (labels 0,1,3, checked by `decide`). Additional scratch checks (not in the file): the wrong K3 labeling 0,1,2 is refuted; the butterfly graph (two triangles sharing a vertex, m = 6) is accepted as near-graceful with labels 0,1,4,5,7 and a bad labeling is refuted.

/-!
# Rosa's conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia, Graceful labeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_labeling)

Rosa's conjecture concerns graceful and near-graceful labelings of triangular cacti.
-/

namespace RosasConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/-- The absolute difference of the labels at the endpoints of an edge. -/
def edgeDifference {V : Type*} (f : V → ℕ) (e : Sym2 V) : ℕ :=
  e.lift ⟨fun u v ↦ Int.natAbs ((f u : ℤ) - (f v : ℤ)), fun u v ↦ by
    show ((f u : ℤ) - f v).natAbs = ((f v : ℤ) - f u).natAbs
    rw [← Int.natAbs_neg, neg_sub]⟩

/-- A finite graph is graceful if its vertices have distinct labels in $\{0,\ldots,m\}$,
where $m$ is its number of edges, and its edge differences are exactly $\{1,\ldots,m\}$. -/
def IsGraceful {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Prop :=
  let m := G.edgeFinset.card
  ∃ f : V → ℕ, Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ v, f v ≤ m) ∧
    G.edgeFinset.image (edgeDifference f) = Finset.Icc 1 m

/-- A finite graph is near-graceful if its vertices have distinct labels in
$\{0,\ldots,m+1\}$ and its $m$ edge differences are distinct members of
$\{1,\ldots,m+1\}$. -/
def IsNearGraceful {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Prop :=
  let m := G.edgeFinset.card
  ∃ f : V → ℕ, Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ v, f v ≤ m + 1) ∧
    Set.InjOn (edgeDifference f) G.edgeSet ∧
    ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, edgeDifference f e ∈ Set.Icc 1 (m + 1)

/-- A triangular cactus is a connected graph all of whose blocks are triangles. Equivalently,
it has an edge, every edge belongs to exactly one triangle, and every graph-theoretic cycle has
length three. -/
def IsTriangularCactus {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  G.Connected ∧ G.edgeSet.Nonempty ∧ G.LocallyLinear ∧
    ∀ ⦃v : V⦄ (c : G.Walk v v), c.IsCycle → c.length = 3

/--
**Rosa's conjecture:** Every finite triangular cactus is graceful or near-graceful. Here a
triangular cactus is a connected graph whose every block is a triangle. If it has $m$ edges,
a graceful labeling injectively labels its vertices in $\{0,\ldots,m\}$ with edge differences
exactly $\{1,\ldots,m\}$; a near-graceful labeling uses $\{0,\ldots,m+1\}$ and has $m$ distinct
edge differences in $\{1,\ldots,m+1\}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem rosas_conjecture {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hG : IsTriangularCactus G) :
    IsGraceful G ∨ IsNearGraceful G := by
  sorry

end RosasConjecture
modeling_decisions: Encoded the cited Wikipedia statement literally as `IsGraceful G ∨ IsNearGraceful G`, rather than replacing it by the logically weaker-looking but equivalent near-graceful conclusion or by Rosa's sharper modulo-4 formulation, neither of which is the cited list-entry wording.

Modeled a triangular cactus by the standard equivalent cycle characterization: the graph is connected and has an edge, every edge lies in exactly one triangle (`SimpleGraph.LocallyLinear`), and every `Walk.IsCycle` has length three. The nonempty-edge clause translates the block condition at the zero-triangle boundary; it excludes the connected singleton whose block is not `K₃`, while retaining the one-triangle cactus.

Used the number `m = G.edgeFinset.card` of undirected edges. Graceful labelings are injective natural-valued vertex labelings bounded by `m` whose image of edge differences is exactly `{1,...,m}`. Near-graceful labelings are injective vertex labelings bounded by `m+1` whose edge-difference function is injective on `G.edgeSet` and takes values in `{1,...,m+1}`.
Represented edge differences with `Int.natAbs` after coercing natural labels to integers, ensuring the endpoint order of an undirected `Sym2` edge is irrelevant.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Rosa's conjecture

Rosa's conjecture states that all triangular cacti are graceful or nearly graceful.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Graceful labeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_labeling)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- A. Rosa, *Cyclic Steiner Triple Systems and Labelings of Triangular Cacti*,

- J. A. Gallian, *A Dynamic Survey of Graph Labeling*, Electron. J. Combin., DS6.

namespace RosasConjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]

/-- The label that a vertex labeling `f` induces on an edge: the absolute difference
$|f(u) - f(v)|$ of the labels of its two endpoints. -/
def edgeLabel (f : V → ℕ) : Sym2 V → ℕ :=
  Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => Nat.dist (f u) (f v), fun u v => Nat.dist_comm (f u) (f v)⟩

/-- A vertex labeling `f` of `G` is a *graceful labeling with bound `N`* if
* no two vertices share a label, i.e. `f` is injective,
* the vertex labels lie in $\{0, \dots, N\}$,
* the induced edge labels $|f(u) - f(v)|$ lie in $\{1, \dots, N\}$, and
* the induced edge labels are pairwise distinct, so that each edge is uniquely identified by
  its label.

Graceful labelings of a graph with $m$ edges are the case `N = m`; near-graceful labelings are
the case `N = m + 1`. -/
def IsGracefulLabelingWithBound (N : ℕ) (f : V → ℕ) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ v, f v ≤ N) ∧
    (∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, edgeLabel f e ∈ Set.Icc 1 N) ∧ G.edgeSet.InjOn (edgeLabel f)

/-- A graph `G` with $m$ edges is *graceful* if its vertices can be labeled with distinct
integers from $\{0, \dots, m\}$ such that the induced edge labels $|f(u) - f(v)|$ are pairwise
distinct and lie in $\{1, \dots, m\}$ (equivalently, they are exactly $1, \dots, m$). -/
def IsGraceful : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℕ, IsGracefulLabelingWithBound G G.edgeFinset.card f

/-- A graph `G` with $m$ edges is *nearly graceful* (or *near-graceful*) if its vertices can be
labeled with distinct integers from $\{0, \dots, m + 1\}$ such that the induced edge labels
$|f(u) - f(v)|$ are pairwise distinct and lie in $\{1, \dots, m + 1\}$. -/
def IsNearGraceful : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℕ, IsGracefulLabelingWithBound G (G.edgeFinset.card + 1) f

/-- A *triangular cactus* is a connected graph all of whose blocks are triangles.

Since Mathlib has no notion of blocks, we use the equivalent description: `G` is connected,
every edge of `G` lies in a triangle, and every cycle of `G` is a triangle (has length `3`).
Under this description a triangular cactus with $t$ triangles has exactly $3t$ edges; the
one-vertex graph is the degenerate triangular cactus with $t = 0$. -/
def IsTriangularCactus : Prop :=
  G.Connected ∧ (∀ u v, G.Adj u v → ∃ w, G.Adj u w ∧ G.Adj v w) ∧
    ∀ ⦃v : V⦄ (c : G.Walk v v), c.IsCycle → c.length = 3

variable {G}

/-- Every graceful graph is nearly graceful. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsGraceful.isNearGraceful (h : IsGraceful G) : IsNearGraceful G := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hle, hrange, hinj⟩ := h
  exact ⟨f, hf, fun v => (hle v).trans (Nat.le_succ _),
    fun e he => Set.Icc_subset_Icc_right (Nat.le_succ _) (hrange e he), hinj⟩

variable (G)

/-- A single triangle is a triangular cactus. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isTriangularCactus_triangle : IsTriangularCactus (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) := by
  refine ⟨connected_top, by decide, fun v c hc => ?_⟩
  refine le_antisymm ?_ hc.three_le_length
  have h₁ := hc.support_nodup.length_le_card
  have h₂ := c.length_support
  simp only [List.length_tail, Fintype.card_fin] at h₁ h₂
  omega

/-- A single edge is not a triangular cactus. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isTriangularCactus_edge : ¬ IsTriangularCactus (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) := by
  rintro ⟨-, h, -⟩
  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := h 0 1 (by decide)
  fin_cases w <;> simp at hw

/-- A single triangle is graceful, with labels `0`, `1`, `3`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isGraceful_triangle : IsGraceful (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) := by
  refine ⟨![0, 1, 3], ?_⟩
  simp only [IsGracefulLabelingWithBound, Set.InjOn]
  decide

/-- The labeling `0`, `1`, `2` of a triangle is not graceful: two edges get the label `1`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isGracefulLabelingWithBound_triangle :
    ¬ IsGracefulLabelingWithBound (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) 3 ![0, 1, 2] := by
  simp only [IsGracefulLabelingWithBound, Set.InjOn]
  decide

/-- **Rosa's conjecture** (Rosa, 1988): every triangular cactus is graceful or nearly graceful.

Here a *triangular cactus* is a connected graph all of whose blocks are triangles. A graph with

  e.lift ⟨fun u v ↦ Int.natAbs ((f u : ℤ) - (f v : ℤ)), fun u v ↦ by

  let m := G.edgeFinset.card

/-!
# Rosa's conjecture

Rosa's conjecture states that all triangular cacti are graceful or nearly graceful.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia/Graceful_labeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_labeling)
- [Wikipedia/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- A. Rosa, *Cyclic Steiner Triple Systems and Labelings of Triangular Cacti*,
  Scientia 1 (1988), 87–95.
- J. A. Gallian, *A dynamic survey of graph labeling*,
  [Electron. J. Combin., DS6](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/DS6).
-/

namespace RosasConjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*}

/-- The label `|f u - f v|` induced on the edge `s(u, v)` by a vertex labelling `f : V → ℕ`. -/
def edgeLabel (f : V → ℕ) : Sym2 V → ℕ :=
  Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => Nat.dist (f u) (f v), fun u v => Nat.dist_comm (f u) (f v)⟩

@[category API, AMS 5]
lemma edgeLabel_mk (f : V → ℕ) (u v : V) : edgeLabel f s(u, v) = Nat.dist (f u) (f v) :=
  rfl

variable [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]

/-- A graph $G$ with $m$ edges is *graceful* if its vertices can be labelled by pairwise distinct
integers in $\{0, \dots, m\}$ such that the induced edge labels $|f(u) - f(v)|$, over the edges
$\{u, v\}$ of $G$, are exactly the integers $1, \dots, m$. -/
def IsGraceful : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℕ, Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ v, f v ≤ G.edgeFinset.card) ∧
    G.edgeFinset.image (edgeLabel f) = Finset.Icc 1 G.edgeFinset.card

/-- A graph $G$ with $m$ edges is *nearly graceful* if its vertices can be labelled by pairwise
distinct integers in $\{0, \dots, m + 1\}$ such that no two edges receive the same induced label
$|f(u) - f(v)|$. The edge labels then automatically lie in $\{1, \dots, m + 1\}$. -/
def IsNearlyGraceful : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℕ, Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ v, f v ≤ G.edgeFinset.card + 1) ∧
    Set.InjOn (edgeLabel f) G.edgeSet

/-- A *triangular cactus* is a connected graph all of whose blocks are triangles.

We encode this as: `G` is connected, every cycle of `G` has length `3`, and no edge of `G` is a
bridge. Indeed, if all cycles are triangles then no two cycles share an edge, so every block of
`G` is a single edge or a triangle, and the bridge condition rules out single-edge blocks. -/
def IsTriangularCactus : Prop :=
  G.Connected ∧ (∀ ⦃v : V⦄ (c : G.Walk v v), c.IsCycle → c.length = 3) ∧
    ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ¬ G.IsBridge e

/-- Every graceful graph is nearly graceful. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
lemma IsGraceful.isNearlyGraceful (h : IsGraceful G) : IsNearlyGraceful G := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf, hle, himage⟩ := h
  refine ⟨f, hf, fun v => (hle v).trans (Nat.le_succ _), ?_⟩
  rw [← coe_edgeFinset, ← Finset.card_image_iff, himage]
  simp

/-- The complete graph `K₃` is graceful. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
lemma isGraceful_top_fin_three : IsGraceful (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) := by
  refine ⟨![0, 1, 3], by decide, by decide, ?_⟩
  decide

/-- The one-vertex graph is a triangular cactus (with no triangles). -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
lemma isTriangularCactus_bot_unit : IsTriangularCactus (⊥ : SimpleGraph Unit) := by
  refine ⟨⟨fun _ _ => Reachable.refl _⟩, fun v c hc => ?_, by simp⟩
  cases c with
  | nil => exact absurd rfl hc.ne_nil
  | cons h _ => exact h.elim

/-- The butterfly graph: two triangles sharing the vertex `0`. It is the triangular cactus with
two triangles, and it is not graceful. -/
def butterfly : SimpleGraph (Fin 5) :=
  fromEdgeSet {s(0, 1), s(0, 2), s(1, 2), s(0, 3), s(0, 4), s(3, 4)}

instance : DecidableRel butterfly.Adj := by
  unfold butterfly
  infer_instance

/-- The butterfly graph is nearly graceful. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
lemma isNearlyGraceful_butterfly : IsNearlyGraceful butterfly := by
  refine ⟨![0, 7, 5, 4, 3], by decide, by decide, ?_⟩
  rw [← coe_edgeFinset, ← Finset.card_image_iff]
  decide

/--
**Rosa's conjecture.** Every triangular cactus (a connected graph all of whose blocks are
triangles) is graceful or nearly graceful.

Here a graph with $m$ edges is *graceful* if its vertices can be labelled by distinct integers in
$\{0, \dots, m\}$ so that the edge labels $|f(u) - f(v)|$ are exactly $1, \dots, m$, and *nearly
graceful* if its vertices can be labelled by distinct integers in $\{0, \dots, m + 1\}$ so that the
edge labels $|f(u) - f(v)|$ are pairwise distinct (they then lie in $\{1, \dots, m + 1\}$).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem rosas_conjecture (hG : IsTriangularCactus G) : IsGraceful G ∨ IsNearlyGraceful G := by
  sorry

/--
Rosa's original formulation of the conjecture (Rosa, 1988) is sharper. Let $G$ be a triangular
cactus with $t$ triangles. If $t \equiv 0, 1 \pmod 4$ then $G$ is graceful, and if
$t \equiv 2, 3 \pmod 4$ then $G$ is nearly graceful (in the sense of `IsNearlyGraceful`).

Such a $G$ is Eulerian with $m = 3t$ edges, so for $t \equiv 2, 3 \pmod 4$ one has
$m \equiv 1, 2 \pmod 4$ and $G$ is not graceful by Rosa's parity theorem.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem rosas_conjecture.variants.mod_four [DecidableEq V] (hG : IsTriangularCactus G) :
    let t := (G.cliqueFinset 3).card
    (t % 4 = 0 ∨ t % 4 = 1 → IsGraceful G) ∧
      (t % 4 = 2 ∨ t % 4 = 3 → IsNearlyGraceful G) := by
  sorry

end RosasConjecture

Definition of 'nearly graceful' follows the Wikipedia article: injective f : V → {0..m+1} with pairwise distinct edge labels |f u - f v| (Set.InjOn on the edge set). The literature (Rosa 1988 / Gallian's survey) may define 'nearly graceful' more restrictively (edge labels {1..m} or {1..m-1, m+1}); the Wikipedia version is a priori weaker and is what the cited source states. Reviewers should check this if the literature definition is preferred; it would affect the variant most.

Definition of 'graceful' follows the standard form (and the existing repo file Wikipedia/GracefulLabeling.lean): injective f : V → {0..m} whose induced edge labels are exactly Finset.Icc 1 m. Wikipedia's phrasing (distinct edge labels in [1,m]) is equivalent since there are m edges.
Edge label |f u - f v| is implemented as `Nat.dist (f u) (f v)` lifted to Sym2 (Nat.dist n m = n - m + (m - n) = |n - m|).

Triangular cactus ('connected graph all of whose blocks are triangles') is encoded without a notion of blocks as: G.Connected ∧ every cycle walk has length 3 ∧ no edge is a bridge (SimpleGraph.IsBridge; equivalently every edge lies on a cycle). Justification: if all cycles are triangles, two distinct triangles cannot share an edge (they would form a 4-cycle), so each edge is in at most one cycle, hence G is a cactus whose blocks are K2's or cycles; bridgelessness excludes K2 blocks and cycle blocks are triangles. Conversely every cycle of a triangular cactus lies in a block (a triangle) and every edge lies in a block (a triangle), so it is not a bridge.

Boundary cases: the empty graph is excluded by G.Connected (requires Nonempty V). The one-vertex graph K1 satisfies the encoded IsTriangularCactus vacuously (0 triangles); under some conventions K1 is not a triangular cactus, but K1 is graceful (m = 0, f = 0), so its inclusion does not change the truth of either theorem. No extra ad hoc hypotheses were added, per the decomposition notes.
Graph is assumed finite via [Fintype V] and edge counting uses G.edgeFinset.card (needs [DecidableRel G.Adj]); [DecidableEq V] is only needed for cliqueFinset in the variant.

A bespoke test graph `butterfly` (two triangles sharing a vertex, the smallest non-graceful triangular cactus) was added with an explicit DecidableRel instance to test IsNearlyGraceful by `decide`; tests also cover K3 graceful and K1 a triangular cactus, plus the API lemma IsGraceful → IsNearlyGraceful.

/-!
# Rosa's conjecture

Rosa's conjecture states that all triangular cacti are graceful or nearly-graceful.

A *triangular cactus* is a connected graph all of whose blocks are triangles. Equivalently,
it is a connected graph in which every edge lies on a cycle and every cycle has length three.

A *graceful labeling* of a graph with $m$ edges is an injective labeling of the vertices by
integers in $\{0, \dots, m\}$ such that the absolute differences of the labels of the endpoints
of the edges are exactly $\{1, \dots, m\}$. A *near-graceful labeling* of a graph with $m$ edges
is an injective labeling of the vertices by integers in $\{0, \dots, m + 1\}$ such that the
absolute differences of the labels of the endpoints of the edges are pairwise distinct (these
differences then lie in $\{1, \dots, m + 1\}$).

Rosa's original form of the conjecture is sharper: a triangular cactus with $t$ triangles is
graceful when $t \equiv 0, 1 \pmod 4$, and when $t \equiv 2, 3 \pmod 4$ (where it cannot be
graceful by Rosa's parity theorem for Eulerian graphs) it has a labeling from
$\{0, \dots, m + 1\}$ with edge labels $\{1, \dots, m - 1, m + 1\}$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Graceful labeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graceful_labeling)
- [Wikipedia, Cactus graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cactus_graph)
- A. Rosa, *Cyclic Steiner triple systems and labelings of triangular cacti*,
  Scientia, Ser. A, Math. Sci. 1 (1988), 87–95.
-/

namespace RosasConjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*}

/-- The label that a vertex labeling `f` induces on an edge `e`: the absolute difference
$|f(u) - f(v)|$ of the labels of its endpoints. -/
def edgeLabel (f : V → ℕ) : Sym2 V → ℕ :=
  Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => ((f u : ℤ) - f v).natAbs, fun u v => by
    show ((f u : ℤ) - f v).natAbs = ((f v : ℤ) - f u).natAbs
    rw [← Int.natAbs_neg, neg_sub]⟩

@[simp, category API, AMS 5]
lemma edgeLabel_mk (f : V → ℕ) (u v : V) : edgeLabel f s(u, v) = ((f u : ℤ) - f v).natAbs :=
  rfl

/-- A *triangular cactus* is a connected graph all of whose blocks are triangles. Equivalently,
it is a connected graph in which every edge lies on a cycle (i.e. no edge is a bridge) and
every cycle has length three. -/
def IsTriangularCactus (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  G.Connected ∧ (∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ¬ G.IsBridge e) ∧
    ∀ (v : V) (p : G.Walk v v), p.IsCycle → p.length = 3

variable [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]

/-- A *graceful labeling* of a graph `G` with `m` edges is an injective map
`f : V → {0, …, m}` whose induced edge labels are exactly `{1, …, m}`. -/
def IsGracefulLabeling (f : V → ℕ) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ v, f v ≤ G.edgeFinset.card) ∧
    G.edgeFinset.image (edgeLabel f) = Finset.Icc 1 G.edgeFinset.card

/-- A graph is *graceful* if it admits a graceful labeling. -/
def IsGraceful : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℕ, IsGracefulLabeling G f

/-- A *near-graceful labeling* of a graph `G` with `m` edges is an injective map
`f : V → {0, …, m + 1}` whose induced edge labels are pairwise distinct. Since the vertex
labels are distinct and lie in `{0, …, m + 1}`, the edge labels automatically lie in
`{1, …, m + 1}`. -/
def IsNearGracefulLabeling (f : V → ℕ) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective f ∧ (∀ v, f v ≤ G.edgeFinset.card + 1) ∧
    Set.InjOn (edgeLabel f) G.edgeSet

/-- A graph is *near-graceful* if it admits a near-graceful labeling. -/
def IsNearGraceful : Prop :=
  ∃ f : V → ℕ, IsNearGracefulLabeling G f

variable {G}

@[category API, AMS 5]
lemma IsGracefulLabeling.isNearGracefulLabeling {f : V → ℕ} (hf : IsGracefulLabeling G f) :
    IsNearGracefulLabeling G f := by
  obtain ⟨hinj, hle, himage⟩ := hf
  refine ⟨hinj, fun v => (hle v).trans (Nat.le_succ _), ?_⟩
  rw [← coe_edgeFinset, ← Finset.card_image_iff, himage]
  simp

/-- Every graceful graph is near-graceful. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
lemma IsGraceful.isNearGraceful (h : IsGraceful G) : IsNearGraceful G :=
  h.imp fun _ hf => hf.isNearGracefulLabeling

/-- The one-vertex graph is a (degenerate) triangular cactus with no triangles. -/

  cases p with
  | nil => exact absurd rfl hp.ne_nil
  | cons h _ => exact absurd h (by simp)

/-- The one-vertex graph is graceful. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
lemma isGraceful_bot_unit : IsGraceful (⊥ : SimpleGraph Unit) :=
  ⟨fun _ => 0, fun _ _ _ => rfl, fun _ => Nat.zero_le _, by simp⟩

  refine ⟨connected_top, fun e _ => ?_, fun v p hp => ?_⟩
  · induction e using Sym2.ind with | _ u v
    rw [isBridge_iff_adj_and_forall_cycle_notMem]

    rw [Walk.cons_isCycle_iff]

    · simp [Walk.isPath_def, hwu, hwv.symm, huv'.symm]
    · simp [huv', huv'.symm, hwu.symm, hwv.symm]
  · refine le_antisymm ?_ hp.three_le_length
    have := hp.support_nodup.length_le_card

  intro u p hp _
  have h1 := hp.three_le_length
  have h2 := hp.support_nodup.length_le_card
  simp [Walk.length_support] at h2

      butterfly.edgeFinset.image (edgeLabel f) = Finset.Icc 1 (m + 1) \ {m} :=

end RosasConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The table correctly notes that Wikipedia's 'graceful or nearly-graceful' (with Wikipedia's weak near-graceful notion) is weaker than Rosa's original mod-4 form; I encoded the literal Wikipedia reading in the slot `rosas_conjecture` and added Rosa's sharper form as a separate variant declaration rather than choosing only one.
modeling_decisions: Triangular cactus ('connected graph all of whose blocks are triangles') is encoded without a block/2-connectivity notion (absent from Mathlib) as: G.Connected ∧ (no edge of G is a bridge, i.e. every edge lies on a cycle) ∧ (every cycle, as a Mathlib `Walk.IsCycle`, has length 3). This is the Wikipedia 'Cactus graph' characterization ('each cycle has length three and each edge belongs to a cycle') and is equivalent to the block definition (a 2-connected block on ≥ 4 vertices containing a triangle has a cycle of length ≥ 4 by the fan lemma; a 2-connected block on 3 vertices is K3; bridges are excluded). Reviewer should check this equivalence.

Near-graceful follows the Wikipedia article literally: labels in {0..m+1}, injective, edge differences pairwise distinct (Set.InjOn on the edge set); the range condition 'differences in [1, m+1]' is automatic and hence not repeated. This is weaker than Rosa's own 'nearly graceful' (edge labels exactly {1,…,m−1,m+1}), so the main theorem is the (weaker) Wikipedia reading. The literal disjunction 'graceful or near-graceful' is kept even though graceful ⇒ near-graceful (proved as an API lemma).

A second declaration `rosas_conjecture.variants.rosa_1988` states the sharper original form: with t = number of triangles (= number of 3-cliques = number of blocks), t ≡ 0,1 (mod 4) ⇒ graceful, and t ≡ 2,3 (mod 4) ⇒ there is an injective labeling into {0..m+1} whose edge labels are exactly Finset.Icc 1 (m+1) \ {m} = {1,…,m−1,m+1}. The exact form of Rosa's 'nearly graceful' was taken from the literature as recalled (Rosa 1988 / Moulton 1989 / Gallian's survey) and is consistent with Rosa's cyclic-STS(6t+1) motivation and with the Eulerian parity constraint; the paper itself was not available in the sandbox, so a reviewer should confirm this definition.

The single-vertex graph satisfies IsTriangularCactus (t = 0, no blocks) and is graceful, so no extra nondegeneracy hypothesis was added, as requested by the decomposition notes; the empty graph is excluded by connectedness.
Vertex type is an arbitrary Fintype (finite graphs), with DecidableRel G.Adj to form edgeFinset; DecidableEq V is only required in the variant for `cliqueFinset`.

Test/API lemmas: graceful ⇒ near-graceful; K1 and K3 are triangular cacti and graceful; K2 is not a triangular cactus; the butterfly graph (t = 2, m = 6, non-graceful) has a Rosa-nearly-graceful labeling 0,2,7,1,4 with edge labels {1,2,3,4,5,7}, checking the t ≡ 2,3 branch of the variant.

$\{1, \dots, m\}$, and near-graceful if there is an injective vertex labeling
$f : V \to \{0, \dots, m + 1\}$ whose induced edge labels are pairwise distinct
(and hence lie in $\{1, \dots, m + 1\}$).
